outbound_official.notes: Singapore's MFA publishes individual country travel-advisory pages for Singapore citizens at https://www.mfa.gov.sg/travelling-overseas/travel-advisories-notices-and-visa-information/ (186 countries as of 2025-2026). There is NO single consolidated visa-free countries list page; visa information is embedded within each country's travel advisory page. The MFA explicitly states this list is 'provided solely as a guide' and recommends travelers verify with the relevant embassy before departure. The country entries above are representative samples confirmed from MFA page snippets returned in web searches. Full coverage requires reading all 186 individual country pages. The MFA pages are the Singapore government's authoritative outbound visa information source.

All travellers (any nationality) also submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival (eservices.ica.gov.sg) - a digital arrival declaration, not a visa.

All travellers (any nationality) also submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival (eservices.ica.gov.sg) - a digital arrival declaration, not a visa.

Holders of ordinary passports issued by the PRC are exempted from visa requirements for stays of up to 30 days. Effective 9 February 2024, pursuant to the mutual 30-day visa-exemption arrangement announced at the 19th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation. All travellers (any nationality) also submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival (eservices.ica.gov.sg) - a digital arrival declaration, not a visa.

US passport holders (regular, official and diplomatic) do not require a visa to enter Singapore for business or social visit purposes. Duration of stay determined by Visit Pass issued at entry. All travellers (any nationality) also submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival (eservices.ica.gov.sg) - a digital arrival declaration, not a visa.

visa_free.nationality: All nationals not listed on the ICA visa-required country list
visa_free.notes: Singapore's ICA publishes a list of countries/territories whose nationals REQUIRE a visa; all other passport holders are visa-exempt. The ICA page states that holders of passports/travel documents NOT from visa-required countries do not need a visa. Stay duration (14, 30, or 90 days) is determined by the Visit Pass issued at the checkpoint. Visa-required countries as of June 2026: Afghanistan, Algeria, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Egypt, Georgia, India, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Moldova, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tunisia, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Yemen. Additionally, holders of refugee travel documents, alien's passports, Palestinian Authority passports, UAE temporary passports, Hong Kong SAR Document of Identity, Macao SAR Travel Permits, and PRC Travel Documents require visas. All travellers (any nationality) also submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival (eservices.ica.gov.sg) - a digital arrival declaration, not a visa.

e_visa.nationality: People's Republic of China (certain travel document holders)
e_visa.notes: PRC nationals holding PRC Travel Documents (not ordinary/diplomatic/public affairs/service passports) may apply for e-Visa via SAVE system. Ordinary passport holders are visa-free as of 9 February 2024. All travellers (any nationality) also submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival (eservices.ica.gov.sg) - a digital arrival declaration, not a visa.

visa_policy.notes: Singapore's ICA publishes a list of countries requiring visas; all other nationalities are visa-exempt and receive a Visit Pass on arrival (14, 30, or 90 days depending on nationality). The official ICA page does not enumerate all visa-free countries by name - it only lists visa-required countries. A 96-hour Visa Free Transit Facility (VFTF) is available: (1) for India and selected PRC nationals who also hold a valid visa/long-term pass from Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, UK, or USA; (2) for CIS, Georgia, Turkmenistan, and Ukraine nationals who hold a valid onward air ticket - NO third-country credential is required for this second group.

credential.issuer: Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, United Kingdom, or United States of America
credential.subtype: any valid visa or long-term pass with at least 1 month remaining validity

conditional_access.conditions: 96-hour Visa-Free Transit Facility (VFTF). Must hold a valid visa or long-term pass issued by and/or good for entry into Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, United Kingdom, or United States of America, with validity of at least one month from date of entry into Singapore under VFTF. Must have valid onward air ticket departing within 96 hours. Must enter Singapore in transit to/from a third country. May enter by any mode but must depart by air or sea. Extension of stay strictly not allowed.

credential.issuer: Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, United Kingdom, or United States of America
credential.subtype: any valid visa or long-term pass with at least 1 month remaining validity - applicable only to PRC nationals NOT holding ordinary, diplomatic, public affairs or service PRC passports

conditional_access.conditions: 96-hour Visa-Free Transit Facility (VFTF) for selected PRC nationals NOT holding ordinary, diplomatic, public affairs or service PRC passports - specifically holders of PRC Travel Documents, Hong Kong SAR Documents of Identity, and Macau SAR Travel Permits. Must hold a valid visa or long-term pass issued by and/or good for entry into Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, United Kingdom, or United States of America, with validity of at least one month from date of entry into Singapore under VFTF. Must have valid onward air ticket departing within 96 hours. Must enter Singapore in transit to/from a third country. May enter by any mode but must depart by air or sea. Extension of stay strictly not allowed.

96-hour Visa-Free Transit Facility (VFTF) for CIS nationals, Georgia, Turkmenistan, and Ukraine. NO third-country visa credential required. Must hold a valid onward air ticket departing Singapore within 96 hours. Must depart Singapore by air. Extension of stay strictly not allowed. Must have sufficient funds for the stay.
Holders of diplomatic, official and service passports issued by India do not need a visa for entry into Singapore. Duration of stay determined by Visit Pass issued at entry.

Holders of diplomatic, public affairs and service passports issued by the PRC are exempted from visa requirements for a stay of up to 30 days in Singapore under long-standing bilateral arrangements, subsequently affirmed through an exchange of diplomatic notes following the 19th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation on 7 December 2023.

Citizens of Saudi Arabia holding diplomatic passports are exempted from Singapore visa requirements. Effective 1 January 2007. All other passport types (ordinary, service, official) still require a visa.

cbi.notes: Singapore does not offer any citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme. The Global Investor Programme (GIP) grants only Permanent Resident (PR) status, not citizenship. Singapore does not permit dual citizenship for adults - persons who obtain another nationality must renounce Singapore citizenship. The ICA confirmed 'The Government has no plans to allow dual citizenship at this juncture.' Source: https://www.ica.gov.sg/news-and-publications/newsroom/media-release/306

programs.name: Global Investor Programme (GIP) – Option A: Direct Business Investment
programs.notes: Grants Singapore Permanent Residency. Invest SGD 10 million in a new or existing Singapore business entity. Must hire minimum 30 employees with at least 50% Singapore Citizens. Minimum 10 new employees required for Re-entry Permit renewal eligibility after initial 5-year period. Application fee S$20,000 (revised 5 May 2025) plus S$100 ICA immigration processing fee. Processing approximately 12 months. After 2 years as PR, applicants aged 21+ may apply for Singapore citizenship (not guaranteed). Changes effective March 15, 2023.

programs.name: Global Investor Programme (GIP) – Option B: GIP-Select Fund Investment
programs.notes: Grants Singapore Permanent Residency. Invest SGD 25 million in a GIP-select fund as shortlisted by EDB. Investment must be demonstrated within 6-month period of Approval-in-Principle (AIP) PR status, made from personal bank account in sole name at a Singapore-registered bank. Application fee S$20,000 (revised 5 May 2025). Processing approximately 12 months. After 2 years as PR, applicants aged 21+ may apply for Singapore citizenship (not guaranteed). Changes effective March 15, 2023.

programs.name: Global Investor Programme (GIP) – Option C: Single-Family Office
programs.notes: Grants Singapore Permanent Residency. Requires minimum SGD 200 million Assets-Under-Management in a Single-Family Office, with a minimum deployment of SGD 50 million in EDB-specified investments (SGX-listed companies, qualifying debt securities, Singapore-licensed managed funds, or private equity in non-listed Singapore businesses) to be deployed no later than 12 months from Final Approval of PR. Application fee S$20,000 (revised 5 May 2025). Processing approximately 12 months. After 2 years as PR, applicants aged 21+ may apply for Singapore citizenship (not guaranteed). Changes effective March 15, 2023.

programs.name: Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass (ONE Pass)
programs.eligibility: Fixed monthly salary of at least S$30,000 for 12 consecutive months with an established company (market cap US$500M+ or annual revenue US$200M+), OR prospective employment at S$30,000/month with an established Singapore company, OR outstanding achievements in sports, arts and culture, or academia/research assessed holistically by MOM
programs.notes: Personalised pass for top talent across all sectors. 5-year validity, renewable for further 5-year periods. No employer sponsorship required. Pass holders can concurrently be employed, run businesses, be directors, or be consultants in multiple Singapore companies. Renewal requires average S$30,000/month salary over 5 years in Singapore OR operating a Singapore company employing at least 5 locals at prevailing EP minimum salary. From January 2027, a new ONE Pass (AI and Tech) track will be introduced (replacing Tech.Pass) allowing salary criterion to be met through a combination of cash and non-cash components (e.g. ESOPs) - confirmed in COS 2026 foreign workforce policy factsheet.

programs.name: Tech.Pass
programs.eligibility: Last drawn fixed monthly salary of at least S$22,500 in the last 1 year, AND at least 5 cumulative years of leadership experience in the past 10 years in a technology company valued at US$500M+ or that raised US$30M+ in funding, OR a venture capital firm managing US$500M+ AUM. 500 places available on first-come, first-served basis.
programs.notes: 2-year validity, renewable once for another 2 years (maximum 4-year total). No employer sponsorship required. Holders can start and operate companies, be an employee, consultant or director in multiple Singapore companies, and mentor start-ups. Tech.Pass is currently still active (as of June 2026) but will be replaced by the ONE Pass (AI and Tech) track from January 2027 per COS 2026 announcement.

programs.name: EntrePass
programs.eligibility: Must register a private limited company with ACRA with at least 30% ownership that is venture-backed or owns innovative technologies. Must meet at least one entrepreneurial track record criterion: raised minimum SGD 100,000 from a single funding round; supported by government-recognized or internationally-renowned incubator/accelerator; previously founded and sold a technology business; holds registered IP providing significant competitive advantage; maintains active research collaboration with Singapore institutions; owns IP registered with an approved national IP institution.
programs.notes: Administered by Ministry of Manpower (MOM). Targets serial entrepreneurs, high-calibre innovators, and experienced investors wanting to operate in Singapore. Certain businesses ineligible (coffee shops, bars, massage parlours, employment agencies, geomancy businesses). EntrePass holders are eligible for PR through the Professionals/Technical Personnel and Skilled Worker scheme administered by ICA.

programs.name: Employment Pass (EP)
programs.eligibility: Candidates must earn at least S$5,600 a month (minimum as of 2025; higher for older, more experienced candidates - up to S$10,700/month at age 45+ for non-financial services, S$11,800/month for financial services). Must pass Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS) unless salary exceeds S$22,500/month. COMPASS evaluates salary relative to local benchmarks, qualifications, diversity, and support for local employment.
programs.notes: Singapore's primary work pass for professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs). Requires employer sponsorship. Holders may eventually apply for PR after residing in Singapore. Current minimum: S$5,600/month (general sectors, age 23 base) up to S$10,700/month (age 45+); S$6,200/month (financial services, age 23 base) up to S$11,800/month (age 45+). From 1 January 2027 (new applications), minimum qualifying salary increases to S$6,000/month base (general sectors) or S$6,600/month base (financial services); renewal threshold increases apply from 1 January 2028.

agreements: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) – Singapore is a founding member; no formal ASEAN-wide freedom of movement agreement exists, but Singapore has bilateral visa-free arrangements with all ASEAN member states

gaps: ICA's official visa requirements page lists only visa-REQUIRED countries (34 as of June 2026, re-confirmed June 2026-06-27). Does not enumerate all visa-free nationalities explicitly; visa-free status is inferred by absence from the required list. Specific stay durations (14/30/90 days) for individual visa-free nationalities other than those explicitly confirmed are not stated verbatim on the official ICA page.

GIP Option A/B/C minimum investment amounts sourced from the EDB GIP page and media releases; the GIP Factsheet PDF (May 2025) could not be parsed from binary encoding. Amounts (SGD 10M / SGD 25M / SGD 200M AUM) are consistent with prior verified sources and 2025 search results.
Processing times for ONE Pass, Tech.Pass, and EntrePass are not explicitly stated on their respective official MOM/EDB pages.
Singapore does not publish an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization) scheme.
No visa-on-arrival facility exists for Singapore.
Max stay days for US nationals and most other visa-free nationalities not explicitly stated on official pages - ICA states the Visit Pass determines duration at entry.
ICA visa requirements page is an interactive SPA; the complete country-by-country list with specific stay durations for all nationalities was not fully extractable via WebFetch.

OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) cardholders: no special entry privilege for Singapore found on any official Singapore government source (ica.gov.sg, mfa.gov.sg). OCI status is not a basis for Singapore entry benefit.

Comprehensive bilateral diplomatic/service passport visa exemption list for Singapore not published as a single official document. Only China (ordinary/diplomatic/public affairs/service - ica.gov.sg), India (diplomatic/official/service - ica.gov.sg), and Saudi Arabia (diplomatic only - ica.gov.sg/789) are explicitly confirmed from official sources. Many other bilateral diplomatic-passport exemptions likely exist but are not confirmed from official Singapore government pages.

Singapore does not have a 'Schengen visa' exemption per se for VFTF; Germany and Switzerland appear individually as qualifying VFTF credential issuers. The ICA VFTF page does not use the word 'Schengen'.

Myanmar diplomatic/official passport exemption: the original ICA SAVE e-visa announcement (media release 637) mentioned Myanmar diplomatic and official passports are exempt, but Myanmar ordinary passport holders have been visa-free since December 1, 2016 (ICA media release 66). The ICA visa-detail page for Myanmar (404 as of June 2026 WebFetch check) could not be independently confirmed for current status of diplomatic vs. ordinary passport distinction.

COS 2026 foreign workforce policy factsheet (PDF, mom.gov.sg) could not be parsed from binary encoding; Tech.Pass → ONE Pass (AI and Tech) replacement mentioned in prior validation notes only via MOM search results. The live MOM ONE Pass eligibility page (fetched 2026-06-27) does NOT mention the ONE Pass (AI and Tech) track - it only refers to 'Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass'. Claim not confirmed from live official page; retained in notes but treated as unverifiable until official page updates.

Wikipedia Visa Policy of Singapore page describes visa-required countries split into Assessment Level I (CIS, Georgia, India, Moldova, North Korea, Turkmenistan, Ukraine + special travel document holders) and Assessment Level II (Afghanistan, Algeria, Bangladesh, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kosovo, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Palestine, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Tunisia, Yemen + UAE temporary passports and Middle Eastern refugee documents). The 'Palestine' classification in Assessment Level II maps to 'Palestinian Authority passports' in the ICA official page (a travel document type, not a nationality per se). No correction needed to visa_required list.

Myanmar visa-free status for Singapore entry: confirmed still in effect as of 2026-06-27. Myanmar's suspension of TOURIST visas (April 2025, earthquake-related) applies only to Myanmar issuing visas for foreigners travelling TO Myanmar - it does not affect Myanmar nationals entering Singapore. ICA media release 66 visa-exemption arrangement remains valid.

visa_types.name: Social Visit Visa
visa_types.notes: Required only for visa-required nationalities; most nationalities are visa-exempt and receive a 30- or 90-day Visit Pass on arrival. The same entry visa covers both social and business visits. Single-journey visa fee is S$30 (about US$22), non-refundable, payable online by Visa/Mastercard. Apply online via the ICA e-Service or through a local contact/authorised visa agent/Singapore Overseas Mission. (Prior official_url returned a 404; updated to the live ICA 'Check if You Need an Entry Visa' page.)

visa_types.name: Employment Pass (EP)
visa_types.purpose: Working in Singapore as a professional, manager, or executive
visa_types.notes: Minimum fixed monthly salary of SGD 5,600/month (general sectors, age 23 base), higher for older candidates (up to SGD 10,700/month at age 45+) and for financial services (SGD 6,200/month base, up to SGD 11,800/month at age 45+). Employer applies on behalf of candidate via EP Online. Total government fee is SGD 330: SGD 105 application fee plus SGD 225 issuance fee (an additional SGD 30 Multiple Journey Visa fee applies for candidates from visa-required nationalities). Confirmed on mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass/apply-for-a-pass; prior figure of SGD 105 only reflected the application fee, omitting the mandatory issuance fee.

visa_types.name: S Pass
visa_types.purpose: Mid-level skilled workers earning at least SGD 3,300/month (SGD 3,800 in financial services)
visa_types.notes: Minimum qualifying salary from 1 September 2025: SGD 3,300/month (general sectors) and SGD 3,800/month (financial services), rising with age up to SGD 4,800 / SGD 5,650 at age 45+. Increases again to SGD 3,600 / SGD 4,000 base for new applications from 1 January 2027. Quota- and levy-based (companies capped at a sector dependency ceiling). Employer applies via EP Online. Total government fee is SGD 205: SGD 105 application fee plus SGD 100 issuance fee, confirmed on mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/s-pass/apply-for-a-pass (prior figure understated the total).

visa_types.name: Student's Pass
visa_types.purpose: Full-time study at a Singapore government school or approved institution
visa_types.notes: Apply via SOLAR (Student's Pass Online Application & Registration) system. Fee SGD 30 for in-principle approval + SGD 60 for issuance.

visa_types.name: Tech.Pass
visa_types.purpose: Established tech entrepreneurs, leaders, and technical experts (salary at least SGD 22,500/month or equivalent track record)
visa_types.notes: Requires last drawn fixed monthly salary of at least SGD 22,500 in the last year, AND 5+ cumulative years in a leading role at a technology company valued US$500M+ or with US$30M+ funding, or at a VC firm with US$500M+ assets under management. Valid 2 years, renewable once (max 4 years); 500 places on a first-come basis. Not tied to an employer. Singapore does not offer a dedicated digital-nomad/remote-work visa; Tech.Pass is a tech-talent work pass. Fee not published on the EDB page. To be superseded by a new ONE Pass (AI and Tech) track from January 2027.

visa_types.name: Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass (ONE Pass)
visa_types.purpose: Top talent across all sectors - fixed salary of at least SGD 30,000/month, or outstanding achievements in arts, sports, science or academia; not tied to an employer
visa_types.notes: Personalised 5-year pass, renewable. No employer sponsorship required; holder may concurrently start, operate and work for multiple Singapore companies. From January 2027 a new ONE Pass (AI and Tech) track is expected to be introduced.

visa_types.name: Personalised Employment Pass (PEP)
visa_types.purpose: High-earning professionals not tied to any single employer
visa_types.notes: To apply, fixed monthly salary of at least SGD 22,500; to keep the pass, at least SGD 270,000 in fixed annual salary per calendar year. Valid up to 3 years, issued once and non-renewable. Holder must not be unemployed for more than 6 months and cannot start a business or freelance.

visa_types.name: EntrePass
visa_types.purpose: Foreign entrepreneurs starting and operating a venture-backed or innovative company in Singapore
visa_types.notes: New pass and first renewal valid up to 1 year; subsequent renewals up to 2 years. No minimum salary or levy/quota, but the company must be ACRA-registered with the applicant holding at least 30% and must meet innovation/funding criteria (e.g. raised at least SGD 100,000). Administered by MOM.

visa_types.name: Work Permit (for migrant workers)
visa_types.purpose: Semi-skilled migrant workers in the construction, manufacturing, marine shipyard, process and services sectors
visa_types.notes: Valid up to 2 years, tied to the worker's passport validity, security bond and employment period. Applicant must be aged 18 to below 62. Employer or appointed agent applies; sector-based quotas (dependency ceilings) and monthly levies apply, and workers come only from approved source countries/regions.

visa_types.name: Training Employment Pass (TEP)
visa_types.purpose: Foreign professionals or students undergoing practical training in professional, managerial, executive or specialist jobs
visa_types.notes: For trainees earning a fixed monthly salary of at least SGD 3,000, or foreign students whose training attachment is part of their course at an acceptable institution. Valid up to 3 months and not renewable. Employer applies.

visa_types.name: Work Holiday Pass (Work Holiday Programme)
visa_types.purpose: Students and young graduates who want to work and holiday in Singapore for up to 6 months
visa_types.notes: Open to undergraduates and graduates aged 18 to 25 from recognised universities in Australia, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and the United States. Valid up to 6 months, non-renewable; capped at 2,000 pass holders at any one time.

visa_types.name: Work Holiday Pass (Work and Holiday Visa Programme)
visa_types.purpose: Australian and New Zealander students and graduates who want to work and holiday in Singapore for up to 12 months
visa_types.notes: Separate from the 6-month Work Holiday Programme; issued under bilateral Work and Holiday visa arrangements. Valid for 12 months.

visa_types.name: Dependant's Pass (DP)
visa_types.purpose: Legally married spouse and unmarried children under 21 of eligible Employment Pass, ONE Pass, Personalised Employment Pass or S Pass holders
visa_types.notes: Validity is tied to the principal pass holder's pass (up to 2 years). The sponsor must earn a qualifying minimum salary. DP holders who wish to work need a Letter of Consent.

visa_types.name: Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)
visa_types.purpose: Common-law spouse, step-children, handicapped children, or parents of an eligible work pass holder who cannot get a Dependant's Pass
visa_types.notes: Validity tied to the principal pass holder (up to 2 years). Parents can be sponsored only if the pass holder earns over SGD 12,000/month. Note: ICA separately issues an LTVP/LTVP+ for foreign spouses of Singapore citizens and permanent residents.

visa_types.name: Visa-Free Transit Facility (VFTF)
visa_types.purpose: 96-hour visa-free transit through Singapore for certain visa-required nationals travelling to/from a third country
visa_types.notes: Free 96-hour transit granted at the checkpoint. India nationals and selected PRC travel-document holders must hold a valid visa or long-term pass for Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the UK or the USA; nationals of CIS countries, Georgia, Turkmenistan and Ukraine need only a confirmed onward air ticket. No extension allowed.

visa_types.name: Miscellaneous Work Pass
visa_types.purpose: Short-term work assignments for eligible foreigners such as conference/seminar speakers, religious workers, or journalists
visa_types.notes: For eligible foreigners on short-term work assignments in Singapore not covered by other passes (e.g. speakers at a seminar/conference, religious workers, journalists). Valid up to 60 days and not renewable. No foreign worker levy or quota required; family passes are not available. Employer or a local sponsor must submit the application via the myMOM Portal. Fee not published on the official MOM overview/key-facts pages.

visa_types.name: Work Permit for Foreign Domestic Worker (FDW)
visa_types.purpose: Migrant domestic workers (MDWs) employed as helpers in private households in Singapore
visa_types.notes: Distinct pass from the general 'Work Permit (for migrant workers)' entry already in this catalog (which covers construction, manufacturing, marine shipyard, process and services sectors); this permit is specifically for domestic helpers employed directly by private households. Valid up to 2 years depending on the validity of the security bond, and renewable. Employer applies via Work Permit Online (WPOL) before and after the worker's arrival; a security bond and medical insurance for the worker are required, and foreign worker levy applies. Exact fee not published on the official MOM overview page.
